subject: Zenova — technical fit recap and agreed next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@zenovahealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@zenovahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Zenova — technical fit recap and action items

Hi Ellen / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap while the details are fresh and a proposal for next steps so we align on scope and timeline. I copied Marissa (SE) to surface technical gaps and propose a workshop.

Top pain points you stated:
- High per-request latency for patient-facing summaries at 1–2s TTL; bursty traffic with periodic peaks during morning shifts.
- Need deterministic cost per 1k completions for forecasting.
- Requirement to run inference under Zenova’s VPC for PHI + KMS-managed keys.
- Desire for structured outputs and reliable reranking for downstream clinical workflow ingestion.

Goals we agreed on:
1) End-to-end prototype that:
   - Accepts EHR text -> calls Redwood streaming generation with structured JSON output (fields: condition, summary, confidence)
   - Uses embeddings + reranker for candidate extraction and sorting
   - Respects Zenova data residency and KMS controls
2) Performance target: 90th percentile latency < 300ms for cached requests; cold path < 800ms for summary length ~120 tokens.
3) A security checklist (SOC2 + VPC setup) to be completed before the pilot.

Technical notes / integration options we discussed:
- SDK: small client-side adapter required (we can provide a 20-line patch) to toggle streaming vs non-streaming endpoints and to add a structured-output schema validator.
- Function calling: recommended for deterministic extraction of discrete fields (we’ll show examples for date, ICD code extraction).
- Embeddings + rerank: best to precompute candidate embeddings for the knowledge store and use a lightweight reranker at inference time to preserve latency SLOs.

Attachments I’ll send with this thread: redwood_integration_compatibility_checklist.xlsx and a short sample Postman collection for our API.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
- Technical workshop (Marissa + 2 engineers) — 60–90 mins — walk through SDK patch, function-calling patterns, and embedding/ rerank flow. Suggested window: Mon/Tue next week.
- Zenova to share SOC2 scope doc + a representative anonymized EHR snippet for schema mapping.
- Redwood to provide an estimated resource baseline and pilot cost range within 48 hours after the workshop.

If that looks right, Ellen — can you confirm the preferred time for the workshop and who from your side will attend?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the clear summary — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

Priorities (order):
1) Data residency & KMS (must be in our US region with customer-managed keys).
2) Deterministic structured outputs for downstream automation (we cannot accept free-text fields).
3) Latency/cost tradeoff — we can tolerate more CPU for higher predictability, but 90th < 300ms is a hard SLO for cached requests.

People for the workshop:
- Rajiv Menon (CTO) — will join and bring our infra lead.
- Priya Shah (Head of Clinical Ops) — will join to validate the structured schema requirements.

We’ll attach (separate email) a SOC2 scoping doc and a small anonymized EHR sample. Also attaching the current Zenova data flow diagram so you can see the ingress/egress points.

Can we do Monday 2025-08-25 at 10:00am PT? That works for our team.

Ellen

Subject: Re: Zenova — technical fit recap and action items

Hi all —

Appreciate the priorities. A few concrete technical follow-ups I’ll bring into the workshop and a short list of pre-work so we can make the 60–90 minute session high-velocity:

1) SDK changes we’ll propose (deliverable: patch + example app)
   - Client toggle: streaming vs response-chunking (minimal surface change).
   - Structured-output validator: schema-first approach using the function-calling/JSON schema pattern — we’ll provide a JS + Python snippet.
   - Retry/backoff config defaults tuned for VPC egress and KMS latency.

2) Function calling patterns
   - Use function-calling to force discrete field extraction (e.g., {"condition":string, "icd10":string, "confidence":number}).
   - Fallback: when confidence < 0.6, return a classification code that signals human review.

3) Embeddings + rerank architecture (high-level)
   - Precompute doc embeddings in a vector DB (we suggest Redis or Milvus); runtime pipeline: query -> topK candidates -> lightweight transformer reranker in Redwood to preserve ordering guarantees.
   - We’ll share benchmark numbers for topK=20 vs topK=50 to show latency/cost tradeoffs (streaming-latency-benchmarks.pdf attached).

4) Security & deployment notes
   - We support VPC private endpoints and customer KMS; Marissa to share a short checklist for network rules and egress exceptions.

Pre-work request from Zenova (to speed the workshop):
- SOC2 scoping doc (for our compliance team).
- One anonymized EHR JSON sample (<=10KB) to sketch schema mapping.
- Confirmation of desired vector DB (if decided) or we’ll recommend one.

Deliverables we will produce within 48 hours after workshop:
- Prototype plan + pilot cost estimate (resource baseline and projected token/embedding costs).
- SDK patch + code examples.
- Checklist for SOC2 + VPC setup.

Looking forward to the session on Mon 2025-08-25 10:00am PT. I’ll bring perf numbers and the SDK diff.

-Marissa
